questions.question: In a zoneless app, a component assigns `this.rate = 84` inside a `setInterval` callback. What happens on screen?
options: The view stays stale because nothing notified Angular to schedule a render
The app falls back to Zone.js automatically
questions.explanation: Without Zone.js, plain property assignments in timers do not schedule change detection. Use a signal or markForCheck().

questions.question: Which of these does NOT schedule change detection in zoneless mode?
options: A signal read in the template changing
A `(click)` listener bound in the template firing
The async pipe receiving a new value
A WebSocket `onmessage` callback assigning a plain class property
questions.explanation: Signals, template event listeners and markForCheck (used by the async pipe) all notify Angular; arbitrary callbacks writing plain properties do not.

questions.question: Why is converting components to `OnPush` a good first step before going zoneless?
options: OnPush components rely on the same explicit notification paths that zoneless mode requires
OnPush disables Zone.js for that component
OnPush is required for signals to compile
Zoneless mode only supports OnPush components
questions.explanation: A component that renders correctly under OnPush already updates via inputs, signals, events or markForCheck, which is exactly what zoneless needs.

questions.question: During zoneless SSR, how do you make the server wait for a custom async data load before serialising HTML?
options: Register it with the PendingTasks service and call the returned cleanup when done
questions.explanation: PendingTasks.add() marks the app as not yet stable; calling the returned function signals the work is complete. HttpClient and the router do this automatically.
